data.name: astryx
data.description: Design system CLI — components, themes, and tooling

globalOptions.description: Simplified Chinese for component reads and for docs topics that have a translation (English otherwise)
Token-efficient dense text for component <Name> and docs <topic> reads
Language or format for component and docs reads: en (default), zh (as --zh), or dense (as --dense)

Detail level for component, hook, and docs tree reads (e.g. docs cli/commands/build), and for theme build reports. Lists default to brief; theme build prints one line per built theme unless full, which adds the install example and font recipe
Output as typed JSON. Success envelope: { apiVersion, type, package?, data, meta? }. Error envelope: { apiVersion, error, code, suggestions? }.

options.description: In the package list, print every component, and every other item, of each package instead of the first 10 and a "+N more" count. No effect on --json output or on a package, component, or search query.

unknown topic or route, a section that matches no section or more than one, or a --depth that is not a number of levels or all

commands.name: gap-report
commands.description: Report a missing component or feature to the package that owns it

arguments.name: component
arguments.description: Component or design-system area the gap is about, up to 120 characters. Required unless --list-categories is set.

options.description: Gap category (run --list-categories for values). Required unless --list-categories is set.
What capability was missing or difficult, up to 2000 characters. Required unless --list-categories is set.
Optional additional context, up to 8000 characters

Package that owns the gap: @astryxdesign/core or a loaded integration. Overrides automatic routing, which picks the integration whose component replaces the named Core component, else the one package that provides it, else Core; needed when more than one package provides the component
Allow public delivery: public handlers run, and a GitHub issues URL gets an issue filed with your gh login
Send the report only to this loaded integration's issues URL, as the person chose; the destinations the output lists are the choices
List valid report categories, and the destinations when there is more than one, without filing; the component and the other gap-report options are refused with ERR_INVALID_ARGUMENT

examples: astryx gap-report Button --category missing_variant --reason 'Need a compact size'
astryx gap-report Button --category missing_variant --reason 'Need a compact size' --to @acme/widgets

exitCodes.when: filed, routed-only, confirmation required, skipped, or categories listed
failed or partial delivery, invalid input, or ambiguous routing

commands.name: init
commands.description: Initialize the design system in your project

options.description: Comma-separated features: agents (agent docs), theme (writes theme.template.ts), template (prints the page-building commands; writes no file). An unknown feature exits 1 with ERR_UNKNOWN_FEATURE. Refused with --all or --remove-agents
Install all features (agents, theme, template); refused with --features. Prints their guidance instead of the getting-started steps

Remove the managed block from AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, .claude/CLAUDE.md, GEMINI.md, .cursorrules, .hermes.md and HERMES.md, at the project root (where init writes them) and in this folder (deleting AGENTS.md or .claude/CLAUDE.md when only init's heading is left, and GEMINI.md when nothing is left) and do nothing else. Below the project root, a project-root agent file whose block resolves outside the project is left as it is, with a note. --features, --all, --agent and --agent-docs-path are refused; a file written with --agent-docs-path keeps its block

Write or refresh the computer-level agent text instead of setting up the folder: one skill file, ~/.agents/skills/astryx/SKILL.md, which most coding agents read, linked into the skill folders of agents that read only their own (~/.claude/skills always; Kiro, Windsurf, Letta, Xcode's coding assistant, and ~/.config/agents/skills when that folder exists): a folder symlink with a relative target, a junction on Windows, or a copy where neither can be made. Continue, whose scanner skips links, gets a managed copy, refreshed with the file. It tells agents anywhere on the computer that Astryx is there, when it is relevant, and to start with `astryx search`. Records the links it made in astryx/settings.json in the per-user configuration folder, so removal removes exactly those; the CLI installed for the computer refreshes the file in the background after each upgrade. Works in any folder. A file without the Astryx markers, one edited since Astryx wrote it, or a symlink, is kept as it is, and so is anything at a link target that Astryx did not create. Warns, and still writes, when no `astryx` command on the computer runs the Astryx CLI. With --remove-agents it removes the file, the links, and the copy instead and records that the text is turned off. --features, --all, --agent and --agent-docs-path are refused

Target AI tool for agent docs: claude (CLAUDE.md or .claude/CLAUDE.md, else creates .claude/CLAUDE.md), cursor (.cursorrules if present, else AGENTS.md), codex and muse (AGENTS.md), hermes (.hermes.md or HERMES.md if present, else AGENTS.md), all (every existing agent doc except GEMINI.md, which keeps its one-line import of AGENTS.md, else AGENTS.md and .claude/CLAUDE.md). With claude and all, when CLAUDE.md gets the block, .claude/CLAUDE.md gets none and a block already there is removed, unless the project ignores CLAUDE.md: then a .claude/CLAUDE.md the project commits gets a copy too, with claude and all alike. An unknown tool exits 1 with ERR_UNKNOWN_AGENT. Used only when agent docs are installed (the default, --all, or --features agents); --agent-docs-path takes precedence.

Explicit file path(s) for agent docs, inside the project; takes precedence over --agent. If any path is outside the project, no agent docs are written and the command exits 1. A path in the home folder itself, or in a settings folder in it outside a project (such as ~/.claude or ~/.claude/hooks), is refused with a note (exit 0), and nothing is written. Used only when agent docs are installed

exitCodes.when: success, including agent docs left unwritten in five soft cases, each reported as docsError with one note: running in the home folder, or in a settings folder in it outside a project; a GEMINI.md that resolves outside the project; when init runs below the project root, a project-root agent file that resolves outside the project; the project's Claude Code file (root CLAUDE.md, or .claude/CLAUDE.md when there is no root one) when it resolves outside the project and is a block-less import of an existing AGENTS.md, which 0.7.1 left alone; and a .claude/CLAUDE.md that resolves outside the project and that 0.7.1 did not write: beside a CLAUDE.md the project ignores, the one --agent claude adds or a block-less import of an existing AGENTS.md; with --agent claude beside a CLAUDE.md, one whose block it would remove

an unknown --agent (ERR_UNKNOWN_AGENT) or feature, an --agent-docs-path outside the project, --remove-agents combined with install options, --user combined with --features, --all, --agent or --agent-docs-path, or --all with --features (ERR_INVALID_ARGUMENT); or, when init runs at the project root, an agent file 0.7.1 also wrote there that resolves outside the project (ERR_PATH_TRAVERSAL, docsError path-safety, nothing written)

commands.name: integration
commands.description: Author and verify an Astryx integration package

exitCodes.when: help is shown or a subcommand succeeds
an unknown subcommand is provided

subcommands.name: integration add
subcommands.description: Add one working contribution to an integration package

arguments.name: kind
arguments.description: component, doc, template, codemod, agent-doc, or theme

arguments.name: name
arguments.description: Contribution name: PascalCase for component (AcmeWidget); lowercase kebab-case for template, codemod, and theme (account-card); letters, digits, _ and - for doc; the literal guidance line for agent-doc

options.description: Validate and show planned writes without changing files
Template type: page (default) or block; only valid for template
Existing doc topic this one replaces (letters, digits, _ and -); only valid for doc and not with --extends
Existing doc topic this one extends (letters, digits, _ and -); only valid for doc and not with --replaces

Namespace of this package to place the doc in, as a guide in its `guides` slot; writes the namespace doc when it is missing, and declares the CLI that reads it as an optional `@astryxdesign/cli` peer. Only valid for doc, and not with --replaces or --extends

Existing theme slug to fork as a starting point instead of a blank scaffold; the new theme copies the base and has no link back, and package.json `dependencies` gains the npm packages the copied files import (other than Core and React). Only valid for theme
Exact semver of the @astryxdesign/core version whose upgrade runs the codemod (e.g. 0.7.0); required for codemod and only valid there

examples: astryx integration add template account-card --type block
astryx integration add doc acme-getting-started --replaces getting-started
astryx integration add doc acme-theming --extends theme
astryx integration add doc releasing --parent acme
astryx integration add agent-doc 'Run acme verify before finishing.'
astryx integration add theme ocean --from neutral

exitCodes.when: the contribution is written or the dry run succeeds
the kind, name, options, package, or target files are invalid or conflict

arguments.name: name
arguments.description: Template id (see --list). Omit it to list the templates.

arguments.name: path
arguments.description: Where to scaffold the template, relative to the project root. A path that ends in .tsx, .ts, .jsx, .js, .mjs, .cjs, .css, .scss, .json, .md or .html is the file to write; any other path is a directory, which receives page.tsx for a page template or the block's own file name for a block. Omit it to print the source.

options.description: List available templates (narrow with --type and --package) and do nothing else: <name>, <path>, --skeleton and --overwrite are refused
Filter by template type: page or block

Replace an existing target file. Without it an existing file is refused (ERR_FILE_EXISTS) and an existing CDN page is left as is

subcommands.description: Compile standalone themes or one keyed theme family

options.description: Build the selected extension family into one keyed CSS, JS, and declaration set, written beside the family root theme file, which must be inside the working directory to build (ERR_PATH_TRAVERSAL); --check only reads, so it compares outputs anywhere. Requires --family-key; refused with --out or --watch (ERR_THEME_INVALID)
Lower-kebab filename stem required with --family and refused without it; must differ from every member name (ERR_THEME_INVALID)

Output CSS file path, relative or absolute; the .js and .d.ts are written beside it (default: <theme name>.css next to the source). A build writes only inside the working directory, the defaults beside the source too (ERR_PATH_TRAVERSAL); --check writes nothing, so it compares outputs anywhere and refuses only a relative path that escapes the working directory. Single theme only: refused with more than one file or with --family (ERR_THEME_INVALID)
Override the icon-registry import in the generated JS module, for example ./icons.mjs (default: the specifier in the theme source's own import). With --family it applies to every member's icon import
Rebuild automatically when a theme file changes (Ctrl-C to stop). Refused with --check, --family, or --json (ERR_THEME_INVALID)
Verify the committed outputs match the source without writing; exit non-zero if stale. Composes with --family and several files; refused with --watch (ERR_THEME_INVALID)

commands.name: upgrade
commands.description: Update your code after upgrading Astryx, and refresh ShadCN-copied components

options.description: Previous version before the dependency upgrade; required unless --list or --registry is set. The target is the installed @astryxdesign/core version, or legacy @xds/core when @astryxdesign/core is not installed
Write changes to disk; without it, the run is a dry run
Run codemods even if --from is newer than the installed version

Run only the named codemod. Optional codemods run only when named here; a normal run skips them. Also skips the check of ShadCN-copied compositions. An unknown name exits 1 with ERR_UNKNOWN_CODEMOD when the version range has codemods
Exclude named codemods (repeatable). Re-run past a failed codemod by skipping it.
Explicit integration specifier (repeatable). Resolved beneath node_modules; absolute paths and `.` or `..` segments are rejected.
Source directory to scan, relative to where you run the command, however you spell it. Without --path, the project's src folder, from any folder in the project
Install jscodeshift when it is missing. Without it, a missing jscodeshift fails the command with ERR_DEP_MISSING

Only update ShadCN-copied compositions from their install receipts: unchanged files are updated, edits that do not overlap are merged, and conflicts are left untouched; --from is not required. Combining it with --list, --from, --force, --codemod, --skip-codemod, --integration or --install-deps exits 1 with ERR_INVALID_ARGUMENT
List available codemods and do nothing else. Every other flag is refused, as is --registry (exit 1)

exitCodes.when: success, including complete dry-run previews

missing or invalid --from, --registry with --list or a migration flag, a --path escape, no installed @astryxdesign/core (or legacy @xds/core), jscodeshift missing and not installed by --install-deps, an astryx.config that fails validation and that no pending config codemod repairs, an unreadable or invalid protection declaration, a protected file that still requires a codemod change, an unknown codemod, a codemod or post-codemod hook failure, or unresolved registry items

globalMode.summary: In a folder that belongs to a project, the project's own CLI answers: this copy hands the run to it. In a project with no CLI of its own, and outside any project, this copy answers. A copy installed for the computer checks the registry for a newer release once a day in the background, and keeps one agent skill file in the home folder.
